# MM-P3-L3-CN02 - Maintenance manual - Machining CNC turning center #2
Revision: Rev E
Plant: P3, line P3-L3
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-CN02

## Scope
This document defines the preventative maintenance tasks required for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02). It covers mechanical inspection, chuck jaw bolt verification, spindle warm-up, and return-to-service checks. Refer to MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1 for parts breakdown and SOP-P3-L3-02 and SOP-P3-L3-04 for safety and lockout procedures.

## Tools
- Torque wrench calibrated per site procedure.
- Basic hand tools and inspection mirror.
- Manufacturer spindle warm-up monitoring tools or machine interface as required.
- Personal protective equipment per SOP-P3-L3-02.

## Procedure
- Perform lockout/tagout per SOP-P3-L3-04 prior to any maintenance on EQ-P3-L3-CN02.
- Visually inspect chuck assembly for wear, debris, and runout as described in MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1.
- Verify chuck jaw bolt torque for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02) is 75 N·m. Use the calibrated torque wrench and apply torque to each bolt in a star pattern until specified torque is achieved.
- Execute spindle warm-up cycle on the machine HMI according to manufacturer guidance. Confirm spindle warm-up time for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02) is 24 minutes. Record start and completion on maintenance log.
- Clean and re-lubricate exterior lubrication points as identified in MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1 using manufacturer-specified lubricants.
- Remove lockout/tagout and return machine to service following SOP-P3-L3-04.

## Acceptance criteria
- Chuck fasteners torqued to the specified value and torque readings recorded on the maintenance record.
- Spindle has completed warm-up and machine reports normal status after the warm-up period.
- No abnormal noise, vibration, oil leaks, or loose components observed on post-maintenance run.
- Maintenance activities documented and cross-referenced to MM-P3-L3-CN02-S1 and relevant SOPs SOP-P3-L3-02 and SOP-P3-L3-04.
